text:
sylvia: Quick q — we're getting some customer reports of 429 spikes on /v1/chat during big bursts. Are we changing the per-route quota header contract for the upcoming rollout? Need guidance to advise SDK folks.

arjun: Not changing the core semantics. Plan is to add an optional per-route hint header (opt-in) that makes burst accounting clearer. Existing global headers stay.

maya: What are the new header names? can we show an exact example so SDKs can parse safely (failing back if absent)? :raised_hands: 

arjun: Example (proposal):
```http
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 12
X-Quota-Global-Remaining: 12345
X-Route-Quota-Remaining: 0  # optional, per-route remaining tokens
X-Route-Quota-Bucket: routes:chat:default  # optional bucket id for client visibility
```

tom: TL;DR: clients must continue to rely on Retry-After and global headers if the new route headers are missing. New ones are best-effort visibility only (not required for correctness).

liz: For backwards compatibility we should:
- keep header names stable
- make route headers optional
- document fallback order in the SDKs

maya: SDK action: parse X-Route-Quota-Remaining if present, else fall back to X-Quota-Global-Remaining, else fallback to Retry-After behavior. Add a metric for how often route header is present.

arjun: Agreed. Also recommend clients treat X-Route-Quota-Bucket as opaque string — only for logging and telemetry. Server side maps buckets to lease windows; clients shouldn't interpret semantics.

deploy-bot: [auto] canary deploy scheduled: per-route quota headers v2 -> canary on 3 hosts at 2026-04-02T15:00Z.

sylvia: Nice. One more: how should we signal soft-429 v.s. hard? We still prefer 200+body {"warning": "degraded"}. If we do 429 for soft cases, include `X-Soft-Throttle: 1` so SDKs can choose to backoff gently. But prefer not to mix.

arjun: We want to avoid new status codes. Option: keep 429 for client-visible throttles. For soft-degrade prefer 200 + body {"warning": "degraded"}. If we do 429 for soft cases, include `X-Soft-Throttle: 1` so SDKs can choose to backoff gently. But prefer not to mix.

tom: Add an SDK flag: on_soft_throttle = "warn" | "strict" so integrators can pick. Document recommended defaults.

maya: I'll draft the SDK PR and the docs patch. sylvia can you confirm if product wants the telemetry field (X-Route-Quota-Bucket) exposed to customers?

sylvia: Expose it as opt-in via a tenant setting. We don't want leaks by default.

arjun: Action items:
- arjun: add server tests and small smoke job verifying headers for burst scenarios (will do today).
- maya: open SDK PR parsing new headers with fallbacks (ETA 2 days).
- liz: update public docs + compat section (ETA EOW).
- sylvia: confirm tenant opt-in gating and security review (ETA tomorrow).

tom: ack. Also let's add a unit test in runtime that simulates a burst from 10k clients and asserts that global fallback behavior is correct (i.e., no client-administered crash if route header missing).

sylvia: Thanks — ping me when PRs are up and I'll coordinate a quick review. :thumbsup:
